summary_en: This controlled phantom study compares conventional 2D B-mode thyroid volumetry with electromagnetically tracked, inertially tracked, and optically tracked 3D ultrasound, alongside CT and MRI. Across six observers, all tracked 3D-ultrasound variants reduced observer dependence and achieved accuracy comparable to CT. The paper is relevant to acoustic imaging and optical-tracking-assisted 3D reconstruction, but it primarily validates established acquisition workflows rather than introducing a new sensing or reconstruction method; candidate status is therefore recommended.
